library(scales)
library(viridis)
library(cowplot) 
library(ggthemes)
library(dplyr)


theme_ps <- function() {
  theme_minimal()+

  theme(
  legend.position = "bottom", 
  panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), # removing major/minor grid lines on x axis
  panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
  panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
  axis.line = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.5),  # adding axis lines and changing color and thickness
  panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.2),  # changing color of the major y axis lines
  plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 17),  # making plot title bold
  plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
  axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.2),  # adding axis ticks 
  axis.ticks.length = unit(0.1, "cm"))}



## Downloading the data

#deliverable 2
  
if (!file.exists("electricity-generation-2026.csv"))
  download.file("https://www.cer-rec.gc.ca/open/energy/energyfutures2026/electricity-generation-technology-2026.csv", destfile = "electricity-generation-technology-2026.csv", mode = "wb")

elec_gen <- read_csv("electricity-generation-technology-2026.csv") %>%clean_names()

# deliverable 3

if (!file.exists("assignment_3_projections.csv"))

ghg_elec <- read_csv("assignment_3_projections.csv") %>%clean_names()

Deliverable 2: Electricity Generation by Source

# Canada graph

elec_gen_can <- elec_gen%>%filter(region == "Canada", 
                                  scenario %in% c("Canada Net-zero","Current Measures"),
                                  variable != "Total") %>%
  mutate(scenario = fct_relevel(scenario, "Current Measures", "Canada Net-zero"))
ggplot(elec_gen_can)+
  geom_col(aes(x = year, y = value/1000, fill = variable), linewidth = 0.25)+
  facet_wrap(~scenario, nrow = 1)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = pretty_breaks(), expand = c(0,0))+
  scale_y_continuous(
  expand = c(0, 0),
  name = "Electricity Generation (TWh)")+
    
  labs(
    title = "National Electricity Generation by Source", x = NULL,caption = "Source: CER Canada's Energy Future, 2026, Graph by Kalathmi Pathiraja", fill = NULL)+ 
scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D")+
  theme_ps()+
  theme(panel.spacing = unit(2, "lines"))

# Alberta Graph
elec_gen_ab <- elec_gen%>%filter(region == "Alberta", 
                                  scenario %in% c("Canada Net-zero","Current Measures"),
                                 variable != "Total") %>%

ggplot(elec_gen_ab)+
  geom_col(aes(x = year, y = value/1000, fill = variable), linewidth = 0.25)+
  facet_wrap(~scenario, nrow = 1)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = pretty_breaks(), expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
  expand = c(0, 0),
  name = "Electricity Generation (TWh)")+
    
  labs(
    title = "Alberta Electricity Generation by Source", x = NULL,caption = "Source: CER Canada's Energy Future, 2026, Graph by Kalathmi Pathiraja", fill = NULL)+ 
scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D")+
  theme_ps()+
  theme(panel.spacing = unit(2, "lines"))

Deliverable 3: Emissions from electricity generation

ghg_elec_inv<-ghg_elec %>% #reorder factor levels
  mutate(prov=fct_relevel(prov,"Canada","BC","AB" ,"SK","MB", "ON","QC","ATL"))%>%
  filter(scenario == "National Inventory Report 2025", prov != "Canada")

ggplot(ghg_elec_inv)+
  geom_area(aes(x = year, y = emissions, fill = prov))+
  scale_x_continuous(
  breaks = seq(2006, 2023, by = 2), expand = c(0,0))+
  
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0,120, by = 10),
                                  limits = c(0,120),
                                  expand = c(0, 0),
  name = expression(Annual~Emissions~(MtCO[2]*e)))+
    
  labs(
    title = "Canadian Electricity Sector GHG Emissions by Province", x = NULL, caption = "Source: Environment and Climate Change Canada, Graph by Kalathmi Pathiraja", subtitle = "2025 National Inventory (1990-2023) Emissions", fill = NULL) + 
  
scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D")+
  theme_ps()+
   theme(plot.margin = margin(5, 15, 5, 5)) 

# projection graph

ghg_elec_proj <- ghg_elec%>% mutate(prov=fct_relevel(prov,"Canada","BC","AB" ,"SK","MB", "ON","QC","ATL")) %>%
  filter(scenario != "2025 With Measures Scenario", prov != "Canada")

ggplot(ghg_elec_proj)+
  geom_area(aes(year,emissions,fill=prov),position = "stack",alpha=.5)+ 
  geom_area(data=filter(ghg_elec_proj,emissions>0 & year<=2023),
            aes(year,emissions,fill=prov), position = "stack",alpha=.8)+
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2023, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2005, 2035, by = 5),
    limits = c(2005, 2035), 
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0,130, by = 10),
  expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0,120),
  name = expression(Annual~Emissions~(MtCO[2]*e)))+
    
  labs(
    title = "Canadian Electricity Sector GHG Emissions", x = NULL, caption = "Source: Environment and Climate Change Canada, Graph by Kalathmi Pathiraja", subtitle = "2025 National Inventory (1990-2023) and 2025 With Additional Measures Scenario projections (2024-2035 lighter fill)", fill = NULL) + 
  
scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D")+
  theme_ps()+
  theme(plot.margin = margin(5, 15, 5, 5))  # Add extra margin on the right

Deliverable 4: The Merit Order

merit_plot <- merit %>%
  filter(date != as.Date("2024-01-10"), he == "19") %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  arrange(price, plant_fuel) %>% # arranges all electricity offers cheapest to most expensive
  mutate(
    size_gw = size / 1000,
    merit = cumsum(size_gw) # adds total supply at the price
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(merit_plot)+
  
# Supply blocks
geom_rect(aes(
  xmin = merit - size_gw,
  xmax = merit,
  ymin = -20,
  ymax = price,
  fill = plant_fuel
)) +

# Vertical line = demand (internal load)
geom_vline(aes(xintercept = alberta_internal_load / 1000, color = "Hourly Internal Load"), linewidth = 1)  +

# Horizontal line = market price
geom_hline(aes(yintercept = pool_price, color = "Mid-Hour Pool Price"), linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_manual(
  values = c(
    "Hourly Internal Load" = "black",
    "Mid-Hour Pool Price" = "red")) +

# Facet by date
facet_wrap(~date, nrow = 1) +
  
scale_x_continuous(
  breaks = seq(0, 12, by = 2),
  expand = c(0,0))+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1000, by = 200),
  limits = c(-20,1000),
  expand = c(0,0))+
  
labs(
  x = "Offered Generation (GW)",
  y = "Price ($/MWh)",
  fill = NULL, color = NULL,
  title = "Alberta Energy Merit Order, select dates in January 2024 at hour ending 7pm",
  caption = "Source: AESO data, Graph by Kalathmi Pathiraja") +
  
scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1")+
theme_ps()
